title: Event and stage lifecycle mutations lack consistent step-up, mandatory reason and two-person controls

original_titles.title: Irreversible finalization and other destructive lifecycle transitions lack step-up and reason
Sensitive organizer operations (stage control, release, time adjust, ledger correction) skip step-up
Finalization gate absent: release not blocked by pending reviews, disputes, or audit-chain verification (RS-03a S1)
Round controls neither broadcast nor typed-confirmation protected (LV-02a S1)
Time adjustments unbounded, no two-person approval (LV-06a S2, ACC-05a)
Live-operation reasons not enforced at >= 10 characters
Reviewer decision reason not required; stage-control reason min length unenforced
Admin UI rules partial: reasons not required for event transitions/dispute resolution, read-only kill switches, no sensitive-data banner, direct-download exports, unpaginated tables
Pause UX partial: no full-width banner, inputs remain editable
Event config edits do not require step-up

problem: set_event_status, control_stage, release_results and time_adjustment use require_organizer rather than a recent step-up dependency. Event status accepts a raw status dict with no reason field; stage control only checks that reason is non-empty; release reason defaults; time adjustments allow ±86400 seconds and have no two-approver policy. The UI uses a two-click ConfirmButton in some places but not typed intent or a mandatory audited reason for every destructive transition.
impact: A stolen organizer session can close/finalize an event, pause/extend/end stages or change participant time without fresh authentication or a sufficiently meaningful explanation. An accidental operator click can become an irreversible event record.

verification.basis: Current source inspection at the main-branch commit listed in metadata. Original audit line numbers are treated as historical and were not reused as current line references.

implementation_steps.action: Define a mutation matrix: low-risk configuration/read operations, operational stage control, and irreversible actions (finalize, archive, publish, release, scoring correction). Document permitted roles for each.
Replace dict bodies with Pydantic request models. Require reason length 10-500, an explicit action, and a typed confirmation phrase for close/finalize/archive/release where appropriate.

Apply step_up_verified to irreversible actions and sensitive time/score operations. Consider two independent approvers for finalization, large time extensions, disqualification and post-release correction.
Write the state change, transition row, announcement/outbox event and audit entry in one database transaction with a correlation/action id.

Add API tests proving organizer without step-up is rejected, empty/short reason is rejected, typed phrase mismatch is rejected, and valid operations create matching transition/audit/announcement records.

acceptance_criteria: No irreversible event/stage/score operation succeeds without the specified role, step-up and reason.
Two-approver operations reject the same approver twice and record both identities.
The participant announcement becomes visible atomically with the operation.
regression_tests: Add a focused failing test before implementation where practical.
Add a negative authorization / boundary test, not only a happy-path test.
Run the affected backend/frontend suite and the full CI workflow before merge.

residual_risk_or_scope_note: PR #59 added step-up to staff/participant registration, team creation/moves/removal, reset, ground-truth changes and manual score adjustment. It did not consistently protect event status, stage control, result release, disputes or time adjustment.
